6251.d:
Based my favourite unsolved problems in Mathematics: the Collatz Conjecture (please search it if you are interested in learning something new).

Each branch of this “tree” corresponds to a unique random number between 2 and 5000. The shape of the branch portrays the behavior of that number according to a simple mathematical rule. So what you are seeing are 100 branches governed purely by Mathematics.
If you look closely, there are two interesting things in the background. First, all the randomly chosen numbers are floating aimlessly on the canvas. Second, there are many tiny mountain-like structures. These are graphs of the numbers (not to scale) and there is a direct relation between the graph and the branch of each number.

This is my attempt to generate something beautiful from pure Mathematics. I hope you like it.

Interactivity:
p :: pause/resume animation
s :: save png
+/- :: Increase/decrease visibility of the floating numbers
RightArrow/LeftArrow :: Increase/decrease the brightness of the graphs.

No libraries were harmed in the making of this code, this is 100% vanilla javascript.

----

Enjoy !

6284.d:
There is a place in 🅗🅞🅝🅖 🅚🅞🅝🅖 full of mystery, where the scents of spices and tiger balm intermingle in a labyrinth of stairs.

🅒🅗🅤🅝🅖🅚🅘🅝🅖 🅜🅐🅝🅢🅘🅞🅝🅢 was built in 1961. The unusual atmosphere of the building complex features guesthouses, curry restaurants, African bistros, clothing shops, sari stores, and foreign exchange offices. It acts as a large gathering place for ethnic minorities in Hong Kong, particularly South Asians, Middle Eastern people and Nigerians.

It is a warm and frightening place that fascinates travellers and an emblematic place of the Hong Kong cinema scene of the 90s. The film Chungking Express by 🅦🅞🅝🅖 🅚🅐🅡 🅦🅐🅘 released in 1994 takes place in the building and tells the stories of two lovesick Hong Kong policeman mulling over their relationship with women.

This series, thought as a tribute to the mystical atmosphere born from the artistic spirit of Wong Kar Wai, brings together a series of glitched drawings of the the dreamy characters of the movie.

Over the centuries, the pandas have become the most powerful species and are defending it against human exploitation. The rivalry between pandas and humans gave rise to a war that was won by the pandas. The humans have now joined forces with the aliens of planet Zuko and plan to annihilate Earth. How are the pandas going to save planet Earth?

6325.d:
A generative abstract painting using layers of strokes of different size, strength and color.

The painting is rendered by simulating one stroke at a time. The recipe is similar for all paintings. First, wide faint brush strokes cover the canvas with a background texture, then a few strong brush strokes give the piece some character. After that, very fine rapid strokes give the piece some interesting detail and finally, dabs of very short brush strokes are applied for additional sense of depth. 

The rendering takes some time. With large screen sizes, you get bigger pictures (for printing!), but the rendering is slower. 

Once the work is painted, you can hit 's' to save a png file. 

There are 7 different colour schemes.

--------------------------------------------------

Features:
Movement: there's 4 different movement types, all with their own meaning and emotion, which you can view in the info tab.
Colors: there's 2 different color schemes, with minor differences in those color schemes to make every piece unique.
Rgb split: when you have a dark background you have a change to split the rgb channels.

- use the mouse to navigate (zoom, pan and drag)
- press 'c' to switch between multiple camera angles
- press 't' to switch time travel mode (use your mouse to go back in time)
- press 'p' in 'Open live' to download the current view it in a custom resolution. This usually results in better quality for prints.

6365.d:
"It is from zero, in zero, that the true movement of being begins." - Kazimir Malevich

120 unique Suprematist revisions inspired by Kazimir Malevich's Suprematist Composition: White on White in 1918 and his first Suprematist spectacle, Black Square in 1915.

Malevich was a Russian avant-garde artist and art theorist, who had a profound influence on abstract art in the early 20th century. Malevich developed the concept of Suprematism as a form of expression that diverged away from the world of natural forms or objectivities and subject matter in art as the only way to gain "the supremacy of pure feeling" and spirituality.

The colors of these revisions and their probabilities are as follow:

Black (~5%) - inspired by Black Square (1915)
White (~15%) - inspired by Suprematist Composition: White on White (1918)
Blue (~10%)
Yellow (~30%)
Red (~40%)

Consider yourself lucky for getting a rare iteration if it is black in color and the square is within the canvas.

Original artwork by Syahmi Rafsan (January 2022)

1 beacon is about the thirty-second most common naturally-occurring oscillator in Achim Flammenkamps census, being slightly less common than the cis-beacon up on long bookend, approximately as common as the cis-beacon on cap, and more common than 20P2. It is the 28th most common oscillator on Adam P. Gouchers Catagolue.

6423.d:
All of my work is about WAVES, and GODS (and quantum mechanics).
https://twitter.com/memotv/status/602195585425403904

I think when I use the term “Waves”, I think I mean the patterns in nature which we humans have managed  -  within our limited cognitive abilities  -  to collectively recognize, decipher and formalize into equations and theories, often that we somehow even find elegant or beautiful - whatever that may mean. And when I use the term “God”, I think I mean those mysterious aspects of nature which we have yet to understand, and the lengths that we will go to, the stories we will tell, to try and make sense of it all. And with the term “quantum mechanics”, I think I mean the fringes of human knowledge, which we empirically know to be quite accurate, and can understand through the language of mathematics. However, we’re not yet able to fully comprehend on a broader, more human level.

I <3 waves :)

See also more incarnations of WAVES on hicetnunc / memoakten

creator: Andrew E. Brereton
date: 2022-01-10
twitter: @aebrer
website: aebrer.xyz
medium: Pico-8, Lua, Tweetcart

This piece uses a type of probabilistic seed resetting to ensure that there will be a seamless loop of random length in each piece. It also makes heavy use of a screen copying technique added to the Pico-8 in version 0.2.4 (the latest). It copies vertical or horizontal bars, and these competing slices make up what you see on the screen, seeded by little hearts :)

Based on this tweetcart I made: https://twitter.com/aebrer/status/1480533290079694861?s=20

Source code:
r=rnd
w=stat(6)
s=1
for i=1,#w do
ch=ord(sub(w,i,i))s+=s*31+ch
end
if(#w==0)s=r(-1) 
srand(s)
function q()return r(32)-16end
pal({q(),q(),q(),q(),q(),q(),q(),q(),q()},1)
f=1_set_fps(60)cls()poke(0x5f54,0x60)::_::
for i=0,9do
?"♥",r(128),r(128),r(10)
end
for i=0,99do
x=r(128)sspr(x,0,1,128,x+r({-1,1}),0,r(2),128)sspr(0,x,128,1,0,x+r({-1,1}),128,r(2))end
if(r(f)>500)srand(s)f=0
f+=1flip()goto _

6482.d:
I've always been fascinated by ammonites. These ancestors of nautilus lived at the same time than the dinosaurs, between 200 and 70 million years ago, and went extinct with them.

There are over 10.000 species of ammonites, with very diverse sizes and shapes. The largest ones ever found were almost 6 ft. across !

I have tried to make these drawings close to real ammonites species, though as always with generative art, you never know what the program will come up with. The scientific names, however, are 100% fictitious, are pay homage to some of the pioneers of the NFT space.

When I was a kid in my native south of France, one of my favorite pastimes was to go fossil hunting. I hope you will, through minting these, somewhat experience the excitement of discovering one of these beautiful pieces hidden inside a rock.
